concepts.def: A substance that can flow. A fluid can be either a liquid or a gas, so gases as well as liquids exert pressure on the surfaces they touch.
The force acting normal to a surface divided by the area of that surface. Pressure is measured in pascals, Pa.
At right angles to the surface. The pressure in a fluid causes a force normal to any surface the fluid is in contact with, whatever the angle of that surface.
The unit of pressure. One pascal is one newton acting normal to each square metre of surface, so 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

concepts.term: Pressure at the surface of a fluid
concepts.def: Calculated with pressure = (force normal to a surface)/(area of that surface), that is p = F/A, with F in newtons and A in metres squared.
The area of the surface over which the normal force is spread. For a fixed force, a larger area of contact gives a smaller pressure.

concepts.term: Pressure due to a column of liquid
concepts.def: Calculated with pressure = height of the column × density of the liquid × gravitational field strength, that is p = h ρ g.
The mass of a material per unit volume, in kilograms per metre cubed, kg/m³. A denser liquid gives a greater pressure at the same depth.
The vertical height of liquid above the point of interest, in metres, m. It is the height of liquid above the point, not the width of the container.
The force of gravity on each kilogram of mass, in newtons per kilogram, N/kg. Its value is given in any calculation in this topic.
The extra pressure between two points in a liquid, found from the difference in height of the two points: Δp = Δh ρ g.
The resultant upward force on a partially or totally submerged object, caused by the pressure on its bottom surface being greater than the pressure on its top surface.
An object floats when the upthrust can balance its weight. An object whose density is less than the density of the liquid floats; a denser object sinks.
A thin layer of air round the Earth, thin compared with the size of the Earth, which gets less dense with increasing altitude.
The pressure caused by air molecules colliding with a surface. It comes from the weight of the air above that surface.
Height above ground level. As altitude increases there is less air above a surface, so atmospheric pressure decreases.

mcqs.q: In physics, what is meant by the term 'fluid'?
options: A substance that can flow: a liquid or a gas.
A liquid only, since a gas cannot be poured.
Anything that pours, such as dry sand.
A gas only, as gases fill any space.
mcqs.explain: The specification states that a fluid can be either a liquid or a gas; both can flow and both exert pressure.

mcqs.q: A sealed can holds compressed air. In which direction does the air pressure exert a force on the flat top of the can?
options: Vertically downwards, pulled by the air's weight.
At right angles to the top, pushing outwards.
Sideways across the top, following the airflow.
Inwards to the centre of the sealed can.
mcqs.explain: The pressure in a fluid causes a force normal to any surface it touches.

mcqs.q: Water in a reservoir presses on a sloping side wall. How does the force from the water act on that wall?
options: Vertically downwards all the way down the wall.
Straight downwards, in line with the water's weight.
Normal to the wall at every point along it.
Along the wall, the way the water runs.
mcqs.explain: Pressure in a fluid causes a force at right angles to the surface, whatever its angle.

mcqs.q: Which equation gives the pressure at the surface of a fluid?
options: pressure = (area of that surface)/(force normal to that surface)
pressure = (force normal to a surface) × (area of the surface)
pressure = (force parallel to a surface)/(area of that surface)
pressure = (force normal to a surface)/(area of that surface)
mcqs.explain: This is the equation exactly as the specification states it: p = F/A.

mcqs.q: A force of 4500 N acts at right angles to a surface of area 0.03 m². Calculate the pressure on the surface.
options: 135 Pa

mcqs.q: A crate presses on the floor with a force of 2400 N normal to the floor and exerts a pressure of 800 Pa. Calculate the area of contact.
options: 3 m²
30 m²

mcqs.q: In the equation p = F/A, what unit is the pressure p measured in?
options: Newton per metre, N/m.
Newtons, written N.
Square metres, m².
Pascals, written Pa.
mcqs.explain: The specification gives pressure, p, in pascals, Pa.

mcqs.q: A force of 16 N acts normal to a surface of area 200 cm². Calculate the pressure in pascals. 1 m² = 10 000 cm²
options: 8 Pa
80 Pa
800 Pa

mcqs.q: A brick of mass 2.0 kg rests flat on a bench. gravitational field strength = 9.8 N/kg  Which value is the force normal to the bench in p = F/A?
options: 19.6 N, the weight of the brick.
2.0 N, the mass rewritten in newtons.
9.8 N, the field strength in N/kg.
0.20 N, the mass divided by g.
mcqs.explain: F must be a force in newtons: weight = 2.0 x 9.8 = 19.6 N.

mcqs.q: A walker on soft snow puts on wide snowshoes and stops sinking in. Why?
options: The larger area increases the pressure on the snow.
The larger area reduces the pressure on the snow.
The larger area presses down harder on the snow.
The force is the walker's mass, and wide shoes shrink it.
mcqs.explain: The normal force is unchanged but is spread over more area, so p = F/A falls.

mcqs.q: Which word equation gives the pressure due to a column of liquid?
options: pressure = width of the column × density of the liquid × gravitational field strength
pressure = height of the column × area of the column × gravitational field strength
pressure = height of the column × density of the liquid × gravitational field strength
pressure = height of the column × density of the liquid / gravitational field
mcqs.explain: This is the word equation exactly as the specification states it.

mcqs.q: In the equation p = h ρ g, how is the height h of the liquid column found from the other quantities?
options: Multiply the pressure by ρ g.
Divide ρ g by the pressure value.
Subtract ρ g from the pressure.
Divide the pressure by ρ g.
mcqs.explain: ρ and g multiply h in p = h ρ g, so h = p divided by ρ g.

mcqs.q: In the equation p = h ρ g, which units must be used for p and for h?
options: p in pascals, Pa and h in centimetres, cm
p in pascals, Pa and h in metres, m
p in newtons, N and h in centimetres, cm
p in newtons, N and h in metres, m
mcqs.explain: The specification gives pressure in pascals, Pa and height of the column in metres, m.

mcqs.q: In the equation p = h ρ g, what unit must the density ρ be given in?
options: Kilograms per metre cubed, kg/m³.
Kilograms per litre, kg/l.
Grams per centimetre cubed, g/cm³.
Newtons per metre cubed, N/m³.
mcqs.explain: The specification gives density, ρ, in kilograms per metre cubed, kg/m³.

mcqs.q: An exam question asks for the pressure at the bottom of a column of sea water. What does the specification say about the gravitational field strength g?
options: It must be recalled from memory as 9.8 N/kg.
It is measured in newtons, N, and is recalled.
It is always taken as exactly 10 N/kg here.
Its value will be given in the question, in N/kg.
mcqs.explain: The specification states that in any calculation the value of g will be given.

mcqs.q: Explain why the pressure at a point in a liquid increases as that point gets deeper.
options: The liquid becomes denser lower down, where it is squashed.
The liquid flows downwards, pressing harder low down.
A taller column of liquid lies above it, weighing more.
The container holds a lot more liquid low down than high up.
mcqs.explain: Pressure is h ρ g: a greater height of liquid above the point means more weight above it.

mcqs.q: Two tanks are filled to the same depth, one with water and one with mercury. Why is the pressure at the base greater in the mercury?
options: Mercury is denser, so the column above weighs more.
The mercury must be filled to a greater depth.
Mercury is denser, so its column is taller than water.
Mercury fills up more volume at the same depth here.
mcqs.explain: In p = h ρ g the height is the same, so the greater density gives the greater pressure.

mcqs.q: Calculate the pressure due to a column of water of height 25 m. density of water = 1000 kg/m³  gravitational field strength = 9.8 N/kg
options: 245 Pa

mcqs.q: A diver swims from a depth of 8.0 m to a depth of 12.0 m. density of sea water = 1030 kg/m³  gravitational field strength = 9.8 N/kg  Calculate the increase in pressure on the diver.
options: 420 Pa

mcqs.q: A sealed can is held completely under water. Why does the water exert a resultant upward force on it?
options: Water pushes up on the bottom and not down on the top.
The can is full of air, which is lighter than the water.
Only the bottom face has water pushing on it.
Pressure on its bottom face exceeds that on its top.
mcqs.explain: The bottom face is deeper, so the pressure there is greater and the resultant force is upwards.

mcqs.q: A submerged object experiences a greater pressure on its bottom surface than on its top surface. What is the resultant upward force called?
options: The force by which upthrust beats weight.
The upthrust on the object.
A normal contact force from the water below.
The water's push under its base only.
mcqs.explain: The specification names this resultant upward force the upthrust.

mcqs.q: A solid block is lowered into a tank of water and floats. Which statement explains why it floats?
options: Its density is lower than the density of the water.
It is lighter than water, whatever its size or shape.
The upthrust on it is larger than its own weight.
It has a large volume and holds a lot of air.
mcqs.explain: Floating and sinking are decided by comparing the density of the object with that of the liquid.

mcqs.q: Which statement best describes a simple model of the Earth's atmosphere?
options: A deep layer of gas that gets denser as altitude rises.
A thick layer of air of the same density at all heights.
A layer of air about as deep as the Earth is wide.
A thin layer of air round the Earth that thins with altitude.
mcqs.explain: The specification describes a thin layer, relative to the size of the Earth, that gets less dense with altitude.

mcqs.q: Explain why atmospheric pressure at the top of a mountain is lower than at sea level.
options: Gravity is much weaker at the top of a high mountain.
The air up there is colder, so it presses down less hard.
There is less air above, so fewer molecules collide.
The wind is stronger high up, blowing the air away.
mcqs.explain: Fewer air molecules above the surface means less weight of air and fewer collisions with it.
